headline: SILVER ROCKETS PAST $80/OZ ON IRAN CEASEFIRE HOPES; SIXTH STRAIGHT SUPPLY DEFICIT PROJECTED AT 67 MILLION OUNCES
snippet: Silver climbed above $80/oz Friday — its highest since mid-March — extending a weekly gain of over 7% as hopes for a US-Iran ceasefire lifted sentiment. J.P. Morgan forecasts a 2026 average of $81/oz as the market heads for its sixth consecutive structural supply deficit, estimated at 67 million ounces, driven by relentless solar-panel and EV demand. Silver has gained more than 150% over the past year.

headline: GOLDSEEK COT REPORT MAY 8: GOLD AND SILVER FUTURES POSITIONING SHIFTS AS PRECIOUS METALS VOLATILITY SPIKES
snippet: GoldSeek's weekly Commitments of Traders analysis for gold, silver, and the US dollar index maps how large speculators are repositioning amid unprecedented precious metals volatility. With gold near $4,750 and silver above $80, the COT data gives clues as to whether the current rally carries speculative excess or still has institutional room to run.

headline: GOLD AT $4,750 AS ANALYSTS SAY HISTORIC RALLY 'COULD RESUME AS FOG OF WAR LIFTS'; MINING EQUITIES STILL LAGGING METAL
snippet: Market watchers say gold and silver's historic rally is far from over despite a mid-week pullback. Gold gained 1.2% to $4,750 while silver added 3% to $79.62 on Thursday as hope mounted for resolution of the 69-day US-Iran conflict. Gold mining equities are up only 35-40% against gold's 60% annual gain — a gap analysts say has to close through a re-rating or M&A.

headline: CHINA BANS SULFURIC ACID EXPORTS FROM MAY; COPPER MINERS FACE SHOCK AS 3 MILLION TONNES VANISH FROM GLOBAL MARKET
snippet: China's halt on sulfuric acid exports — effective May through at least December 2026 — removes roughly 3 million tonnes from the global seaborne market, threatening copper and nickel extraction worldwide. Chile, which imports over 1 million tonnes annually from China for acid-leach copper processing, faces spot-market costs rising 40-60% above pre-ban levels. The disruption compounds war-driven sulfur shortages from the Middle East, where Strait of Hormuz disruption has cut off one-third of global sulfur supply.

headline: COPPER TOUCHES $6.23/LB — UP 35% YEAR-ON-YEAR — AS AI POWER GRID BUILDOUT MEETS DECADE-TIGHT SUPPLY
snippet: Copper futures climbed to $6.23 per pound on May 8, approaching record highs set in January, as investor conviction builds around sustained AI infrastructure, power-grid modernization, and clean-energy demand. Year-on-year gains stand at 35% with supply constraints compounding: sulfuric acid shortages, smelting bottlenecks, and war-driven logistical disruptions are all pressuring the output side simultaneously.

headline: COEUR MINING Q1 POST-NEW GOLD DEAL: $3B EBITDA TARGET, $2B FREE CASH FLOW GUIDE, $750M BUYBACK AUTHORIZED
snippet: Coeur Mining's first quarterly report since completing its $7 billion acquisition of New Gold sets 2026 guidance at over $3 billion EBITDA and $2 billion free cash flow. The board authorized a $750 million share repurchase program and an inaugural semi-annual dividend of $0.02/share. The combined entity now operates seven wholly-owned North American mines and is expected to produce 680,000-815,000 ounces of gold-equivalent in 2026.

headline: SSR MINING Q1 EARNINGS TRIPLE TO $1.15/SHARE; GOLD REALIZED AT $4,770/OZ AS COPLER MINE SALE ADDS $1.5B CASH
snippet: SSR Mining posted a blowout Q1 2026, with earnings nearly tripling year-over-year to $1.15/share on 84% revenue growth to $581 million. An average realized gold price of $4,770/oz — up from $2,935 a year prior — amplified production gains. The company also announced the $1.5 billion sale of its suspended Copler mine in Turkey, expected to close by Q3, sharply derisking the portfolio and improving its North American focus.

headline: FENECK: GOLD PRODUCERS PRINTING RECORD CASH AT $4,700 GOLD — STOCK WEAKNESS OPENING A ONCE-IN-A-DECADE M&A WINDOW
snippet: Analyst John Feneck argues that gold producers generating record free cash flow at $4,700+ gold are still trading at a structural discount to the metal — a gap that historically closes through a valuation re-rating or M&A consolidation. With the GDX up only 35-40% against gold's 60% gain, Feneck calls the current setup the best he has seen in a decade for acquisition-driven upside in mid-tier and junior producers.

headline: URANIUM LONG-TERM CONTRACTS HIT $90/LB — HIGHEST SINCE 2008 — AS UTILITIES LOCK IN SUPPLY AT 60% OVER SPOT
snippet: Long-term uranium contract prices have reached $90/lb — the highest since 2008 — while spot holds near $86/lb. Utilities are no longer price-shopping; they are security-shopping, willing to pay a roughly 60% premium over spot for guaranteed 2028-2030 delivery. AI hyperscalers competing for nuclear baseload power and a Kazatomprom-projected 21-million-pound deficit by 2030 are the twin engines driving the contracting surge.

headline: RARE EARTHS AMERICAS RAISES $63.3M IN FIRST U.S. RARE EARTH IPO SINCE 2010; TARGETS DYSPROSIUM AND TERBIUM
snippet: Rare Earths Americas (NYSE American: REA) priced its upsized IPO at $19/share, raising $63.3 million — the first traditional U.S. rare earth listing since 2010. The exploration-stage company targets heavy rare earths including dysprosium and terbium, critical for high-performance permanent magnets, from projects in Brazil and the state of Georgia. Shares opened 31% above IPO price before closing flat on debut.

headline: NdPr OXIDE FALLS 21% IN APRIL TO $99.61/KG; REMAINS 88% ABOVE JANUARY AS MARKET EYES CHINA QUOTA DUE IN JUNE
snippet: Neodymium-praseodymium oxide suffered its sharpest monthly decline since the Q1 rally began, falling 21% in April to $99.61/kg — though it remains 88% above its January opening price. The market is expected to consolidate in a $95-$115/kg range through Q2. China's mid-year MIIT mining quota announcement — typically released in June — is the next major catalyst that could set the direction for second-half rare earth prices.

headline: ENERGY STORAGE BOOM LIFTS LITHIUM; MORGAN STANLEY SEES 80,000-TONNE DEFICIT IN 2026 AFTER YEARS OF GLUT
snippet: Battery energy storage system deployments are outpacing forecasts, bolstering lithium demand just as inventory buffers shrink. Morgan Stanley projects an 80,000 MT LCE deficit in 2026 — a dramatic swing from an expected 61,000-tonne surplus in 2025. Chile's April lithium carbonate exports surged 175.6% year-over-year to $498 million, confirming that physical off-take is accelerating even as spot prices remain suppressed.

headline: SILVER47 HITS 38.7 G/T GOLD AND 1,713 G/T SILVER AT NEVADA'S KENNEDY PROJECT; 15KM VEIN NETWORK LARGELY UNTESTED
snippet: Silver47 Exploration (TSX-V: AGA) reported rock sample assays of up to 38.7 g/t gold and 1,713 g/t silver from the Kennedy Gold-Silver Project in Nevada — highlighting a 15 km largely untested vein network across a 6,150-acre land package. Management is planning a grid-based soil geochemistry survey of up to 3,000 samples and IP geophysics to sharpen drill targeting. The company also has active drilling at the nearby Hughes Ruby target.
